questions.q: What is the version control discipline test this lesson proposes for a project's committed files?
options: Only sfdx-project.json needs to be committed; everything else is optional
Only Apex classes need to be committed, not config files
A teammate cloning the repo and deploying to their own scratch org should get a working result with zero undocumented manual steps
Commits should happen at most once per week
questions.explain: The test is practical: if something is required for the project to deploy correctly, it has to be in Git — a teammate cloning the repo should be able to deploy successfully with no hidden manual steps.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend deleting scratch orgs when you're done with them instead of letting them passively expire?
options: Expired scratch orgs are more expensive to the organization than deleted ones
Letting them accumulate risks hitting the Dev Hub's active scratch org allocation limit at an inconvenient moment
Passive expiration causes permanent data corruption in the Dev Hub
Only deleted scratch orgs can be converted into org snapshots
questions.explain: Letting unused scratch orgs pile up risks running into the Dev Hub's active scratch org allocation limit right when you actually need to create a new one — deliberate deletion avoids that.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend using to test whether a .forceignore pattern is working as intended, before trusting it?
options: sf package version create
sf org delete scratch
git log
sf project deploy preview, which surfaces exactly what's being excluded
questions.explain: sf project deploy preview explicitly lists what a deploy would exclude due to .forceignore, letting you confirm a pattern does what you intended before relying on it in a real deploy.

questions.q: According to this lesson's packaging guidance, when should you reach for an unlocked package rather than leaving metadata unpackaged?
options: When metadata genuinely needs to move between multiple internal orgs as a versioned unit
Only when distributing commercial software to customers on AppExchange
Every single piece of metadata in every project should always be packaged
Never — unlocked packages are deprecated
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes: unpackaged metadata is fine for org-specific configuration, unlocked packages fit metadata that needs to move between multiple internal orgs as a versioned unit, and managed packages are reserved for distributing software outside your control.

questions.q: What does this lesson say should never be committed to version control, and what's the correct alternative for CI authentication?
options: Apex classes should never be committed; use the Developer Console instead
sfdx-project.json should never be committed; it should be regenerated each time
Credentials/secrets should never be committed; CI authentication uses a JWT-based flow with a connected app and a private key kept out of version control
Scratch org definition files should never be committed; they should be typed manually each run
questions.explain: Authentication should happen through the CLI's own stored connections or, for non-interactive CI use, a JWT-based auth flow using a connected app and a private key kept out of Git — never credentials typed into a committed file.
